Subject: Transport paths: criteria for VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Hi all,

We need a short, decision-ready summary of which transport path(s) we should recommend for BlueMarble's private deployment pilot. Requirements (high level): low tail latency for inference, strong data isolation for regulated PII workloads, straightforward operational ownership for NetOps, and the ability to scale to multi-region later.

Attached: connectivity_criteria.xlsx and a small latency benchmark from last week's lab run. Please review and send concise pros/cons + a recommended default (and a fallback) by EOD Friday.

- Latency (median + p95) impact for short-text token streams
- Data surface area (which connectivity pattern minimizes attack surface)
- Operational effort (routing changes, cross-account approvals, additional endpoints)
- Cost model (bandwidth and endpoint costs)

I'll loop in BlueMarble NetOps (Alex) on constraints. If anyone thinks we should run a quick experiment before deciding, call it out.

Diego — good framework. High level notes below (short bullets so we can synth a matrix):

VPC Peering
- Pros: Lowest hop count and predictable low RTT for intra-cloud traffic; no per-GB PrivateLink fees. Good for high-volume, low-latency inference.
- Cons: Non-transitive (requires pairwise peering if more than two VPCs); cross-account peering needs manual approvals; expands routing table management; harder to lock down to a single service (larger surface).

PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints)
- Pros: Small surface area — only the endpoint + ENI; endpoint policies let you restrict consumer principals; aligns well with regulated workloads and auditing. Easier for compliance teams to reason about.
- Cons: Per-endpoint and per-GB egress costs; each region needs its own endpoint; slightly higher RTT vs peering due to proxy hop. Operationally, needs service owner to publish endpoint service.

Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec)
- Pros: Quick to stand up; works with on-prem customers without cloud peering. Keeps traffic encrypted across public internet.
- Cons: Variable latency, lower throughput, tunnel management overhead and rekeying. Not ideal as primary path for low-latency inference.

Recommendation (draft):
- Default: VPC peering for internal high-volume inference lanes where both sides are cloud VPCs and teams accept broader surface area.
- Sensitive customer lanes (PII/regulatory): PrivateLink with strict endpoint policies + flow logs.
- VPN: DR/fallback and for on-prem customers that cannot peer.

Happy to put this into a short decision matrix.

-kim

Adding empirical numbers from the lab run (attached latency-benchmark-20270621.csv):
- Peering: median RTT 9ms, p95 ~16ms on our test TTL (in-region). Throughput more than sufficient for batching up to 256 tokens at our current model settings.
- PrivateLink: median RTT 14ms, p95 ~24ms (proxy + ENI). Throughput slightly reduced under concurrent streams due to endpoint ENI limits — can be mitigated with endpoint scaling.
- VPN (IPSec over Internet): median RTT 48ms, p95 >80ms in worst runs; throughput and stability fluctuate with ISP.

Operational implication for LLM inference: prefix/KV cache effectiveness degrades if RTT increases (more stalls on cache misses). For customer-facing low-tail-latency use cases we should avoid VPN as primary.

Suggested hybrid:
- Use peering for our internal control/metrics and high-volume non-PII traffic.
- PrivateLink for regulated customers and tenancy isolation (explicit endpoint per customer/project).
- VPN as an allowed fallback for on-prem customers where peering is impossible.

I can update the decision matrix with these numbers.

-Marcus

Thanks — a couple security notes we should fold into the recommendation: 
- PrivateLink simplifies scoping for SOC/audit because traffic terminates at an ENI under our control and endpoint policies can lock down callers. Recommend PrivateLink as the default for any workload with regulated data (PII, PHI).
- For peering, we must define explicit routing filters and avoid broad security groups that open lateral movement; recommended: VPC-level route tables + firewall ACLs + flow logs to SIEM.
- VPN: require multi-factor authentication for tunnel control plane where supported and mandatory IPSec cipher suites (AES256-GCM) in contracts. Also require periodic tunnel monitoring (SLA of 99.9% for production).

Please include compliance in the loop if we land on peering for any regulated customer. Happy to add the endpoint policy template and KMS integration checklist.

-Mina

Thanks for the fast inputs — good alignment and actionable next steps. My summary and actions: 

Summary (consensus):
- Peering: best latency and cost for high-volume cloud-to-cloud lanes, but increases network surface and routing work.
- PrivateLink: preferred for regulated/sensitive traffic due to narrow surface area and endpoint policies; modest latency increase and higher per-GB costs.
- VPN: acceptable as a fallback/DR and for true on-prem customers; not acceptable as primary for latency-sensitive inference.
